> 以正治國，以奇用兵，以無事取天下.

Chapter 56 filed off the point and untied the bundle in one person's chest. Chapter 57 is about a person in charge of a place, and how not to add to it.

Three characters, each with an edge.

## 正 is a foot that has stopped

正 is built on 止 — the foot. Its sense is a foot stopping where it should be: aligned, in place, not moving past.

So 以正治國 is not "govern by righteousness." It is: the governance is aligned, and nothing is stepping past its position.

## 奇 is the unpaired one

奇: 異也，一曰不耦 — odd, and specifically 不耦: unpaired, without a counterpart.

So 以奇用兵 is not "use deception." It is: use the move that has no counterpart — the one thing the other side has not matched. A battlefield is the one place where being unpaired is an advantage, which is why war is the exception and not the model.

## 彰 is a painted pattern

彰 is built on 彡 — three strokes of hair, the mark of a painted design.

So 法令滋彰 is not "many laws." It is: the statutes are being painted more and more elaborately.

## The four consequences

> 天下多忌諱，而民彌貧；民多利器，國家滋昏；人多伎巧，奇物滋起；法令滋彰，盜賊多有.

Four clauses, and each is a causal inversion of the obvious intention.

More prohibitions, and the people are poorer — because prohibitions remove room to act, and room is the resource.

More sharp tools, and the state grows dimmer — because instruments of conflict multiply the conflicts.

More cleverness, and stranger goods arise — because skill that must be displayed needs new objects to display on.

More statutes, and more thieves — because a dense code creates a dense field of things that can be broken.

Note 滋: four times. It means to increase, to proliferate — and it is the same 滋 as in 滋彰. The proliferation is the point: each of these measures grows itself.

## 我無為，而民自化

Four 我 + 自 pairs:

- 我無為，而民自化 — I do not force, and the people transform themselves.
- 我好靜，而民自正 — I keep still, and the people align themselves.
- 我無事，而民自富 — I add no affairs, and the people become sufficient.
- 我無欲，而民自樸 — I want nothing, and the people return to the log.

The repeated 自 is the same 自 as 自然: of themselves. The ruler's contribution in every line is absence.

## 取天下

取, as chapter 48 established, is to cut off an ear for the count.

> 以無事取天下.

Three characters in front of the same verb, and it stops being an ear-taking. 無事 — no affairs added — turns 取 from a seizure into a reception.

Which is the chapter's central claim about power: the same verb, with an interior condition attached, changes the nature of the act.

## Why this is harder than it sounds

The four 自's look passive, and they are the most demanding position in the book.

Not adding affairs is not doing nothing. It requires knowing, precisely, which affairs are yours — and every additional measure feels like responsibility rather than interference.

The four 滋's are what happens when that knowledge is missing: each addition is made in good faith, and each one multiplies itself.

## A test

Take one rule you have added to a system in the last year. Ask what it was meant to prevent, and then count the things it made possible to break. That count is 盜賊多有.
